We believe that we qualify to be taxed as a REIT and as such will not be subject to federal income tax on that portion of our income that is distributed to shareholders as long as we meet applicable REIT asset, income and share ownership tests.

If we fail to qualify as a REIT, and do not qualify for certain statutory relief provisions, our profits will be subject to income taxes and we may be precluded from qualifying as a REIT for the four tax years following the year we lose our REIT qualification.
We expect that the effective rate for the provision for income taxes may be volatile in future periods.

We evaluate our deferred tax assets quarterly to determine if valuation allowances are required based on the consideration of all available positive and negative evidence using a “more-likely-than-not” standard with respect to whether deferred tax assets will be realized.
Our hedging activities are intended to manage our net exposure across all interest rate-sensitive strategies, including MSRs, MBS, and the effects of income taxes on our results.
Realization of expected cash flows is influenced by changes in the level of our servicing assets, changes in estimates of remaining cash flows to be realized, and realized prepayment performance.

Realization of expected cash flows decreased by $4.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting the decrease in the average balance of our MSR portfolio and declining prepayment speeds during the period as interest rates increased.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, realization of expected cash flows increased by $15.8 million compared to the same period in 2025, as faster prepayment activity early in the period more than offset the decrease in the average balance of our portfolio.
Our Net gains on loans held for sale include our estimates of gains or losses we expect to realize upon the sale of mortgage loans we have committed to purchase but have not yet purchased or sold.
The MSRs and liabilities for representations and warranties we recognize represent our estimate of the fair value of future benefits and costs we will realize for years in the future.
We recognize liabilities for losses we expect to incur relating to the representations and warranties we provide to purchasers in our loan sales transactions.

We expect our primary sources of liquidity to be cash flows from our investment portfolio, including cash earnings on our investments, cash flows from business activities, liquidation of existing investments and proceeds from borrowings and/or additional equity offerings.
We expect to continue investing in subordinate MBS generated from non-Agency securitizations which are also expected to increase our VIEs' asset-backed financings.
We expect to reduce the Common Share dividend we declare in the fourth quarter of 2026 to support book value accretion, while continuing to consider the taxable income we are required to distribute.

We make collateralized borrowings in the form of sales of assets under agreements to repurchase, loan participation purchase and sale agreements and notes payable, including secured term financing for our MSRs and our CRT arrangements that have allowed us to match the term of our borrowings more closely to the expected lives of the assets securing those borrowings.

Because a significant portion of our current debt facilities consists of short-term borrowings, we expect to either renew these facilities in advance of maturity in order to ensure our ongoing liquidity and access to capital or otherwise allow ourselves sufficient time to replace any necessary financing.
